A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiMed-ST study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. V2's new abbreviation section is visibly empty, rather than an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original ASR, machine translation, and speech translation experiments, including human evaluations and extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments, human evaluations, and appendix results.

M1.justification: The model architectures, cascaded and end-to-end pipelines, fine-tuning procedures, and prompt templates are retained. The new overview figure introduces no algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MultiMed-ST data, five languages, translation directions, and ASR/MT/ST tasks. Code-switching coverage and dataset statistics are unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the main and appendix experiments is unchanged, including Whisper, commercial ASR systems, encoder-decoder MT models, LLMs, and end-to-end ST models.

E3.justification: Section 2.2 changes unqualified human correction and cross-verification of all translations to an explicitly test-set-scoped description. This substantially narrows the documented human-validation coverage. It does not establish that the underlying data changed or experiments were rerun; other evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The SpecAugment comparison, bilingual/multilingual analyses, code-switch analysis, in-context learning experiments, and quantitative and qualitative error analyses are retained without new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for model results. The reported consensus agreement remains 100%; its scope qualification concerns the annotation protocol.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores and appendix examples are unchanged, but Section 5.2 replaces the claim that M2M100 surpasses LLMs on 18/20 language pairs with 'many language pairs.' The original count is unsupported by the unchanged Table 3.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, MFCC derivations, attention-model equations, training objective, and metric definitions are retained. Differences concern notation spacing, acronym expansions, and figure references.

C1.justification: The principal claims about the first systematic medical ST study, dataset scale and multilingual coverage, and the five conclusions remain substantively unchanged. Stronger visual emphasis and revised adjectives do not introduce new contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly presents consensus filtering as removing bias from LLM-generated translations and removes the acknowledgement's claim of deployment in HYKIST clinical trials. Most explanations and limitations, including Appendix G's annotation discussion, are retained.

D1.justification: Section 2.2 revises the estimated annotation labor cost from USD 290k–580k to USD 29k–58k; actual expenditure remains undisclosed. Appendix model configurations, preprocessing instructions, prompts, and resource links are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Zhang et al. (2021b) on translation-supported teamwork and Zhang and Gao (2024) on migrants' information seeking. The related-work survey and overall novelty positioning otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes local prose and terminology edits, updates affiliations and contribution statements, simplifies Appendix C's heading, and adds an empty abbreviation section. The scientific narrative and main section order are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds overview Figure 1 and broadly revises presentation through colored score emphasis, a ranking legend, caption takeaways, and icons. Table placement and continuation labels change, while existing appendix figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies human-validation coverage and removes the unsupported 18/20 finding, improving reporting precision. However, its new Table 3 legend marks Google's English-to-Vietnamese BLEU of 59.50 as best and M2M100's higher 62.31 as second-best, introducing misleading guidance. The new abbreviation section is also empty. These competing reporting gains and presentation regressions prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
